programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.desc: Cyrus, Darius and Xerxes; these Persian kings are sometimes stereotyped as one-dimensional despots in Greek histories; the truth about the Achaemenid Persian Empire; an empire that stretches from Egypt and Asia Minor, all the way to the Indus Valley.

programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.desc: Greek historians provide valuable information about the Persian Empire; the Greek perspective is often negatively biased; archaeology uncovers inscriptions, administrative tablets and other documents that let the Persians speak for themselves.

programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.desc: The ancient world before the Persian Empire; in the centuries leading up to the Persian Empire, the Assyrians are the major international power; the Assyrian kingdom collapses; it leaves a power vacuum in the region; the stage set for new power.

programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.sub-title: Cyrus and Cambyses - Founders of the Empire
programme.desc: Cyrus, the first great king of the Persian Empire, expands the empire through pragmatic leadership; he uses local customs and traditions and thereby gains legitimacy over Central Asia and Babylon; his son Cambyses expands the empire into Egypt.

programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.sub-title: Darius I - Creator of the Imperial System
programme.desc: Whether Darius, the son-in-law of Cyrus, is a legitimate king; After Cambyses dies, Darius establishes himself as an unwavering leader; Darius creates a royal genealogy and a Persian identity; he then turns to building infrastructure.

programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.desc: The five Persian capitals; Pasargadae, Ecbatana, Babylon, Susa and Persepolis; built in strategic, fortified locations, these cities are major symbols of power for the great kings; exploring the great hall at Persepolis, which holds 10,000 guests.

programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.sub-title: The Great King - Images and Realities
programme.desc: Seeing beyond the outside stereotypes of Persian kings as tyrants; seeing what the kings themselves have to say; in sculpted reliefs and carvings on royal tombs, the words and images of Darius and Xerxes show Persian values of harmonious cooperation.

programme.title: The Persian Empire
programme.desc: A trip into the western provinces; the empire's diverse local customs; the Persian Empire is famous for its roads and bridges; how its express messenger system allows information to travel quickly; the king keeps tabs on every corner of the empire.

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
programme.desc: The geographical region known as Greater Middle East; the range of nations and cultures that define it; historical turning points to witness, encompassing conquests, political alliances and Islam's rise; social, intellectual and economic reforms.

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
programme.sub-title: Muhammad and the Dawn of Islam - 622
programme.desc: Islam's rise is a major turning point; tracing key phases in the life of Muhammad (PBUH); the founding of the faith through his years of opposition; his establishment of Islam as a religious and political entity; the global impact of these events.

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
programme.desc: The seventh-century Arab invasion of North Africa brings profound change to the entire region; the Arab armies of the newly created Islamic empire try to conquer the territories of Egypt and others; the lasting Arabization and Islamization.

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
programme.desc: The establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate's capital in Damascus is a key event in early Muslim history; the Umayyads' achievements; locating the empire's capital away from the Arabian Peninsula; the shift from an Islamic empire to imperial power.

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
programme.desc: The Battle of Karbala represents a key moment in the split between the two main branches of Islam; the faith comes to violent internal conflict early in its history; the dispute over succession; the political and religious fallout from the battle.

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
programme.desc: The events surrounding the incursion of Berber-Arab armies into the Iberian Peninsula in 711; Muslim domination of the region lasts 800 years; the fateful Battle of Guadalete; the Arabs' advance north; the invasion's impact on European history.

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History

programme.title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
